title: Sections with closed support: adjunction and fiber triangle for all coefficients
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring (in particular any admissible one), $i\colon Z\hookrightarrow X$
a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement $j\colon V\hookrightarrow X$, and
$\underline\Gamma_Z(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ for $\Lambda_X$-modules $M$
(as in [def-exc-proetale-sections-with-support], with $\Lambda$ in place of a finite ring).

1. $\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)=i_*\underline\Gamma_Z(M)$, and $\underline\Gamma_Z$ is right adjoint to
   $i_*$ on module sheaves; it is left exact.
2. $R\underline\Gamma_Z$, computed on K-injective complexes, is right adjoint to $i_*$ on
   $D(-_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$; equivalently
   $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*A,K)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A,R\underline\Gamma_ZK)$.
3. For an injective $\Lambda_X$-module $I$, the unit $I\to j_*j^*I$ is surjective.
4. There is a distinguished triangle
   $i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK[1]$, natural in $K$, and
   $R\underline\Gamma_ZK\cong i^*\fib(K\to Rj_*j^*K)$.

proof.text: Work on the small site models in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in the common enlarged universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $B=\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For $a=i,j$, [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] identifies $a^{-1}B$ with $\Lambda_{\operatorname{dom}(a)}$. Thus the coefficient rings on $Z,V$ really are the inverse-image rings, rather than constant rings with scalar ring $\Lambda(*)$. Modules mean left module sheaves in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with their usual sectionwise actions. This description also covers noncommutative ring sheaves; none of the arguments below uses multiplicative commutativity.

source.place: Opening paragraph: pulled-back coefficients; compare def-sfb-alpha and the arbitrary-ring formulation

proof.text: The inverse/direct images on underlying sheaves are those of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Inverse image is exact on abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. Lift these functors to modules by applying inverse image to the action $B\times M\to M$, and giving $a_*N$ the $B$-action through $B\to a_*a^{-1}B$. Apply the adjunction on sheaves of sets to the action maps (which need not be additive on the Cartesian product). The adjunction restricts to linear maps: if $L=a^{-1}$, $R=a_*$ and $\beta=R\alpha\circ\eta_M$, the adjuncts of the two linearity maps $\alpha\circ L\mu_M$ and $\mu_N\circ(1\times\alpha)$ are $\beta\circ\mu_M$ and $R\mu_N\circ(\eta_B\times\beta)$, respectively. This follows from naturality of $\eta$ and its product comparison. Hence equality on one side is equivalent to equality on the other. The unit and counit are linear. Transport along the coefficient isomorphisms of Step 1 changes only the scalar action. Kernels and sheafified cokernels have the underlying abelian kernels and cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; it follows that $i^*,j^*$ are exact. Additivity follows from the sectionwise addition of maps.

source.place: Opening paragraph: exact inverse images and the adjunctions; Stacks Tags 09A5 and 04JC, with the module-linearity calculation written out

proof.text: For the completed clauses use the proved abelian closed-support interface [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-abelian-closed-support] instead of passage through commutative ringed module sheaves. Lift invertibility of its counit and supported units through mapModAdjunction, the scalar-transport equivalence, and the faithful module forgetful functor. The open restriction of a closed direct image is zero by evaluation on empty base changes. For extension by zero use the source-library mapModLeft construction and its exactness; composing its adjunction with inverse scalar transport works for noncommutative monoid objects too. Closed direct image preserves colimits because Step 5 exhibits it as a left adjoint. The exactness helper is restricted to the quasi-compact complementary-open case asserted by this node; there is no unrestricted exactness instance.

proof.text: The source-library localized open restriction/direct-image adjunction has invertible counit. Transfer full faithfulness to the ordinary abelian inverse-image adjunction and then to the scalar-transported module adjunction as in Step 3. The triangle identity makes open pullback of its unit invertible.

source.place: Opening paragraph and (1): open direct-image full faithfulness; Stacks Tag 09BN, localized-site calculation

proof.text: Put N = ker(M -> j_* j^* M). Preservation of kernels and the invertibility in Step 4 give j^* N = 0. Apply the supported-unit assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-abelian-closed-support] to the underlying abelian sheaf and lift it as in Step 3; this proves that the specified kernel comparison is invertible. Every map i_* A -> M has zero composite with the open unit by the open adjunction and j^* i_* A = 0. Factor it through the kernel and apply full faithfulness of i_* to obtain the explicit natural Hom equivalence. Its counit is the fixed kernel inclusion, and Adjunction.ext_counit proves uniqueness. The resulting right adjoint preserves limits. Kernel-map addition is checked by equalizer.hom_ext, so the support functor is additive.

source.place: (1): kernel identification and natural Hom factorization

proof.text: The source-library Mod.isGrothendieckAbelian supplies the module categories and their K-injective resolutions in the stated universes. Use the existing upstream rightDerivedFunctor and exact-left-adjoint derived-adjunction constructions. Identify the recorded arbitrary-quasi-isomorphism-resolution right derived functor with the upstream one by their universal properties: rightDerivedDesc supplies the map on natural transformations, rightDerived_fac its factorization, and rightDerived_ext injectivity. No degreewise-injective replacement is needed for these completed assertions. The completed triangle and fibre assertions instead use the existing formal recollement and mapping-cocone APIs, so no degreewise-injective replacement is needed there either.

proof.text:
By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], exact $i_*$ acts termwise on derived categories. In [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], take $v=i_*$ and $u=H$; Steps 3 and 5 verify the exact-left-adjoint hypotheses, so $H(I)$ is K-injective when $I$ is. For a complex $A$ on $Z$ and a resolution $K\to I$ on $X$, the homotopy adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(i_*A,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(X)}(i_*A,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(Z)}(A,H(I))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z)}(A,RHK).$$
The resolution comparison in Step 6 identifies $H(I)$ with $RHK$. This proves the derived adjunction in (2).

source.place: (2): unbounded derived adjunction; Stacks Tags 015F, 08BJ and 070I

proof.text: Apply the additive sheaf Hom equivalence of Step 5 to each (p,q) component of the global Hom complex. AddEquiv.piCongrRight gives the degreewise additive isomorphism, and HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents assembles it. Expand the Hom differential: naturality of the adjunction in the target handles the first summand, naturality in the source handles the second, and additivity commutes with the integer sign scalar. The component formula is definitional. This proves exactly the displayed Hom-complex isomorphism, without internal-Hom or boundedness claims.

source.place: (2), last sentence: global Hom-complex form of the termwise adjunction; Stacks Tag 070I

proof.text: Use the proved source-library isZero_of_mono_openImmersionLowerShriek (FiniteCoefficient.LowerShriek.Open.Mono), rather than a new localization sequence. Lift the fully faithful abelian extension-by-zero adjunction through mapModLeft and scalar transport; its module unit is invertible. Thus restriction of its counit is invertible. The counit kernel has zero open restriction, and its underlying abelian kernel embeds in an extension by zero. The cited source lemma makes that kernel zero, proving the module counit monic. Put F = j_* j^* I. Extend the map j_! j^* F -> I adjoint to the open counit along the monic extension counit to sigma : F -> I, using injectivity. Applying the extension adjunction shows j^* sigma equals the open counit. Applying the open Hom equivalence and its triangle identity gives sigma followed by the open unit equal to the identity of F. Consequently the open unit is split epic, hence epic. This argument works without using the closed-pushforward exactness assertion.

source.place: (3): extend the open counit along the monic comparison, then check the resulting section

proof.text: Use the proved generic source-library Recollement.existsUnique_distTriang_counit_unit, rather than constructing a short exact sequence of injective complexes. Derive the needed closed direct-image exactness locally from the sheaf support adjunction, under the node's quasi-compact complement hypothesis. Closed and open direct images preserve K-injectives as right adjoints to exact inverse images; [lem-exc-kinjective-derived-fully-faithful] therefore makes their total derived functors fully faithful. Identify the exact closed derived direct image with its termwise mapDerivedCategory. Open restriction of a closed direct image vanishes termwise, so it vanishes in the derived category. Closed and open inverse images jointly detect zero modules: when the open restriction is zero, the supported-unit isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-abelian-closed-support] identifies the module with its closed direct image, which is zero if closed restriction is zero. Since both inverse images commute with homology by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], they jointly detect zero derived objects. Complete the derived closed unit K -> i_*i^*K to a distinguished triangle. Its closed restriction is invertible by full faithfulness and the triangle identity. If j^*K=0 its open restriction is also invertible, between zero objects. Joint detection makes its cone zero; hence the unit is invertible and K is in the essential image of i_*. These are exactly the hypotheses of the generic recollement theorem. It gives the unique connecting arrow completing the specified closed counit and open unit. Recollement.exists_triangleHom identifies the first and third components of every such triangle map with the functors applied to its middle component. Its third commutativity equation proves naturality of the chosen connecting arrows. This proves the required natural transformation and distinguished triangle on the entire unbounded category.

source.place: (4): support triangle; formal recollement proof in the same unit, sk-prop-sf-localization/_section.md; source-library Recollement.existsUnique_distTriang_counit_unit and exists_triangleHom

proof.text: For a K-injective complex I, open restriction j^*I is K-injective by the proved extension-by-zero adjunction. Thus the right-derived unit for j_* is invertible on j^*I. The derived adjunction unit factorization (Adjunction.derivedη_fac_app) compares the derived open unit at QI with Q of the termwise sheaf unit. Transport from the homotopy localization Qh to Q using quotientCompQhIso; its naturality gives an isomorphism of targets identifying the two units exactly. Take the mappingCocone triangle of the actual termwise open unit. Its first vertex is precisely mappingCone(unit I)[-1], and its image under Q is distinguished. Rotate this triangle and the supported triangle from Step 10. Their first two vertices and first arrow agree through the just-proved unit comparison. The standard isomorphism of distinguished triangles with two specified vertex isomorphisms identifies their third vertices; fully faithful shift cancels the common [1], identifying i_*RH(QI) with Q(mappingCone(unit I)[-1]). The derived closed pullback/direct-image counit is invertible by full faithfulness, so apply i^* to this isomorphism and cancel i^*i_*. Finally transport RH along the given K ≅ QI. This proves the stated fibre formula for every K-injective representative without choosing injective terms or changing the canonical unit. All constructions used for this comparison are actual derived units, naturality identities, and distinguished-triangle isomorphisms.

source.place: (4): fibre formula from the support triangle; mapping-cocone triangle and derived-unit factorization, Stacks Tags 0152, 070I and 015F

lean.statement:
theorem closedSupport_triangle {Z U X : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (hij : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ) :
    letI := closedSupport_lowerStarExact Λ i j hij
    ∃ δ : (supportPullback Λ j).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ (lowerStar Λ j).rightDerivedFunctor ⟶
      ((closedSupport Λ i j).rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ (lowerStar Λ i).mapDerivedCategory) ⋙
        shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (supportModules Λ X)) (1 : ℤ),
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory (supportModules Λ X),
        Triangle.mk ((closedSupportDerivedAdjunction Λ i j hij).counit.app K)
          ((closedSupportOpenDerivedAdjunction Λ j).unit.app K) (δ.app K) ∈
            Pretriangulated.distinguishedTriangles
lean.note: The declarations jointly state clauses (1)--(4). The support kernel and pullback are real constructions for every condensed ring, with no commutativity or finiteness hypothesis. Pullback transports the canonical alpha isomorphism by inverse restriction of scalars, extending the commutative upstream API without changing coefficients. The sheaf adjunction is chosen from its unique counit normalization; the derived adjunctions use the existing exact-left-adjoint construction. The global RHom clause is specified on K-injective Hom complexes componentwise, and the fibre is the shifted mapping cone of the actual open unit. The recorded arbitrary-quasi-isomorphism right-derived interface is identified with the upstream universal pair by a unique unit-compatible comparison.
